title: Bucanus: knowledge of Christ, double judgment, heart’s apprehension
source_text: XXIX. Bucanus quoque docet tres esse partes fidem constituentes; sed in earum expositione habet etiam aliquid singulare. Prima pars fidei illi est notitia Christi crucifixi, & beneficiorum ejus. Secunda, consensus, seu judicium duplex; unum generale, approbans tanquam verum quod in verbo Dei de Christo, ejusque beneficiis docetur: alterum speciale, quo sibi credens adjudicat res illas bonas & salutares, quae offeruntur in verbo, hoc est, universales Evangelii promissiones ad se pertinere judicat; ac denique tertia pars est cordis apprehensio, qua fit ut corde & voluntate, tanquam manu apprehendamus, & ambabus ulnis amplectamur, id quod mens nostra, non verum modo, sed etiam sanctum, bonum, & salutare, & ad nos quoque peculiariter pertinere judicavit. Loco 29. quaestione 6.
pass_a_gloss: Bucanus also teaches that there are three parts constituting faith; but in their exposition he has also something singular. The first part of faith for him is knowledge of Christ crucified and of His benefits. The second, consent, or a double judgment: one general, approving as true what is taught in the word of God concerning Christ and His benefits; the other special, by which the believer adjudges to himself those good and saving things which are offered in the word — that is, judges that the universal promises of the Gospel pertain to himself; and finally the third part is the heart's apprehension, by which it comes about that with heart and will, as with the hand, we apprehend, and with both arms embrace, that which our mind has judged not only true, but also holy, good, and saving, and peculiarly pertaining to us also. Place 29, question 6.
pass_b_english: Bucanus: three constituting parts — with a distinctive twist.
1. Knowledge of crucified Christ and His benefits.
2. Consent / double judgment: general approval of Word-truth about Christ; special self-adjudgment that Gospel promises are mine.
3. Heart’s apprehension — will embraces what the mind judged true, holy, good, saving, and peculiarly ours.
